# Simpler career results · 0.36.0

The results page now starts with up to three collapsed career-name accordions. Each contains specific match reasons, visible work preferences, training and program examples, one cost breakdown, entry and 5/10/20-year estimated pay, and a direct lifestyle verdict. Other matches show their rating and a short reason before opening the same details.

The display keeps task evidence and full interest-profile similarity ahead of income. Lifestyle fit breaks ties only within a close evidence tier: identical specialty and route support, identical match basis, a task-score difference of at most one point, and, for profile-supported matches, a correlation difference of at most 0.10. This display selection does not change questionnaire answers, six interest scores, core profession rankings or stored choices. Task-supported careers retain a Task match label when the wider interest profile differs.

## Costs and pay

Hairdressing's existing $44,673 reference is $15,700 tuition, $23,648 living expenses and $5,325 other expenses. It uses the Aveda Austin training reference. Other costs include the kit, fees, health coverage and licensing. Costs now appear together rather than as competing tuition-only and full-budget figures. Source details remain expandable. Where a source does not separate living from other expenses, the combined label remains explicit.

The electrician example uses the published 2025–26 apprenticeship reference of $825 tuition and $35 application fees for one training year. It is not presented as a current whole-apprenticeship quotation. Administrative assistant work has no required college tuition; optional college certificates no longer appear as required training. College estimates identify the Texas-resident UT Austin cost reference even when a separate program example is at another school. The industrial-design program example is the University of Houston BS Industrial Design, four years and 132 credits: https://www.uh.edu/architecture/industrial-design/degree-programs/bsid/.

Pay keeps all four milestones visible under Estimated yearly pay. Source details explain the later modeled amounts. Paid residency, apprenticeship and academy pay and experienced-role prerequisites remain explicit. Repeated planning-estimate labels, lifestyle links and disclaimer paragraphs were removed.

## Navigation and saved work

The five education groups link to relevant careers that meet the selected lifestyle budget at entry. Groups without such an option say No match. Links open the matching career accordion; careers beyond the compact list open their own details. Grants, savings and loan controls have a separate funding page. Existing custom funding entries remain stored and take priority over new defaults.

The main app and isolated student preview use the same renderer. Saved action notes, completion states, earlier career steps and exploration notes remain available behind disclosures. Preview changes remain in memory and never save into the real guide. The six owner-only cases retain their existing authentication and private storage.

## Checks and limits

The frozen replay covers 148 public fictional cases and six owner-only fictional cases. Answers, raw six scores and core engine matches remain unchanged. All 117 training-cost breakdowns are nonnegative and reconcile. Dedicated checks cover compact match selection, task/profile boundaries, visible other-match reasons, cost reconciliation, separate funding controls and nonmutating rendering. Phone testing checks expansion and education links. These checks do not establish matching accuracy or outcomes with real students.

The complete software suite passes 512 tests. Syntax checks and the public-output scan for 79 private biography fragments also pass.
